market_view: Calm regime: VIX 16.5, down 9% in 5 days, and the dollar slightly weaker; chips and metals rallied hard on 08-04 while crude fell 5-6% on Hormuz reopening hopes. Earnings season and the first-Friday jobs report add variance.

oil_gas.catalyst: none (negative headlines: Reuters 'Oil prices mixed as investors ponder Strait of Hormuz reopening hopes'; Reuters 'Trump blasts Exxon, Chevron for making too much money, demands lower gasoline prices')
oil_gas.reasoning: WTI -5.7% on 08-04 and 60d -20%; Hormuz reopening hopes and political pressure on XOM are downside risks. XOM is still up 8.7% over 20 days while crude falls, so there is no one-sided upside setup.

gold_miners.reasoning: Gold +1.5% and NEM +2.5% on lower yields and a softer dollar, but that move is priced. The 10-year yield of 4.63% is near its 1-year high, the jobs report is a two-sided event, and there is no NEM-specific headline.

chips.catalyst: none (CNBC 'Lisa Su brushes off Musk's Nvidia commitment as AMD stock sinks after earnings' is mixed; the NVIDIA blog posts are product news, not catalysts)
chips.reasoning: SOXX +5.6% in one day and +8.7% over 5 days is already priced. AMD slid after earnings and there is no NVDA guidance or export-rule change, so high variance and no named catalyst mean flat.

pharma.catalyst: Eli Lilly press release 'Lilly reports second-quarter 2026 financial results, raises full-year guidance, and highlights continued growth and pipeline progress' (published 2026-08-05 07:00 GMT, after the last close in the record)
pharma.reasoning: A guidance raise is the trigger set in the previous note. LLY fell 8.6% over 5 days into the print, so expectations were cut. The raise came after the last close, so it is not in the price data. Its size is unknown, so confidence is modest.

copper_uranium.catalyst: Continuing from 07-31: CNBC 'Deadly storms and a global supply squeeze are sending copper prices soaring'; copper has since risen another 4.7% in 5 days to 6.62, 0.5% below its 1-year high
copper_uranium.reasoning: Hold the FCX long opened 2026-07-31 (20-day hold ends around 2026-08-28). The supply shock persists, nothing says supply is recovering, and the dollar is weaker. FCX is +9% over 5 days, so further upside is smaller; keep the original exit rules.

would_change_my_mind: Reports of copper mine restarts or a sharp dollar rebound (exit FCX); details of a small or low-quality Lilly guidance raise, or LLY falling on the print (exit LLY); renewed Hormuz closure with crude not yet repriced (XOM long).

handoff.what_changed: Lilly reported Q2 and raised full-year guidance before the 08-05 open after a 5-day drop of 8.6%; opened a LLY long on that catalyst. Crude fell 5-6% on 08-04 on Hormuz reopening hopes, and Trump blasted Exxon and Chevron for making too much money. Copper kept rising to 6.62, near its 1-year high; FCX +9% in 5 days, so the long is held.

oil_gas.why: Hormuz reopening hopes and Trump's pressure on XOM/CVX profits are downside risks; no upside catalyst.

gold_miners.why: Gold bounce on lower yields is priced; the 10-year is near its 1-year high and the jobs report is two-sided.

chips.why: Sharp sector rally is priced; AMD sank after earnings; no NVDA-specific catalyst.

pharma.why: Q2 results with a full-year guidance raise after an 8.6% pre-earnings drop.

copper_uranium.why: Storm and global supply squeeze in copper persists; copper near its 1-year high.
